items.comment: The OT overlay is published only as tables in this PDF. NIST publishes SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and the SP 800-53B baselines that the overlay tailors in OSCAL (usnistgov/oscal-content), but there is no machine-readable version of the SP 800-82 OT overlay. Organizations that manage controls in OSCAL-based or other GRC tooling must re-key the 390 baseline-allocated rows of Appendix E, and their OT Discussions, by hand, and must repeat that work for every revision. An unofficial OSCAL rendering of this draft overlay, generated by script from the PDF, shows that the overlay can be expressed without loss as three OSCAL profiles that import the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 OSCAL catalog: 160 (Low), 304 (Moderate) and 387 (High) controls and control enhancements, with each OT Discussion and each rationale for an added control attached as a profile alteration, and the three removals recorded. The profiles validate with oscal-cli 3.2.0. They are offered as a starting point at https://github.com/Johnbjoseph-cybersec/nist-800-82r4-ot-overlay-oscal.
items.proposed: Publish the final OT overlay as OSCAL profiles (Low, Moderate, High) alongside the SP 800-53B baseline profiles in usnistgov/oscal-content and in the overlay repository cited at line 6830. After line 6832, add a sentence pointing readers to the machine-readable version.

items.comment: The overlay is in Appendix E in this draft (it was Appendix F in Rev. 3). Three references in the RMF appendix still point to Appendix F: line 8294 ("Appendix F of this publication includes an OT-specific overlay"), line 8299 ("tailor the overlay from Appendix F") and Table 21, Task S-1, page 299 ("control baselines identified in Appendix F"). Appendix F is now the RMF appendix itself.
items.proposed: Change "Appendix F" to "Appendix E" at line 8294, at line 8299 and in Table 21, Task S-1.

items.comment: Rev. 3 ended with "Appendix G. Change Log". This draft has no change log (its appendices are A to F), so readers cannot tell what changed from Rev. 3, including in the overlay. A comparison of the detailed overlay tables in Rev. 3 (Appendix F) and this draft (Appendix E) found the same Select, Add and Remove allocation for all 407 control rows: the same 24 additions and the same 3 removals. If that is intended, it is useful for implementers to know that the baselines are unchanged.
items.proposed: Add a change log appendix, as in Rev. 3, summarizing the changes from Rev. 3. For the overlay, state whether the baseline allocations changed, and list any control whose allocation or OT Discussion changed.

items.comment: The text says "Figure 21 uses the AU-4 control as an example", but Fig. 21 (page 218, line 6983) illustrates AC-3 Access Enforcement and its enhancement AC-3 (11). The same sentence appears in Rev. 3 for its Fig. 22.
items.proposed: Change "the AU-4 control" to "the AC-3 control" at line 6967.

items.comment: The example table row after line 6879 reads "AU-4 Audit Storage Capacity". The SP 800-53 Rev. 5 title, also used in Table 18, is "Audit Log Storage Capacity".
items.proposed: Change the example row to "AU-4 Audit Log Storage Capacity".

items.comment: The AU-6 heading at line 7204 uses the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 title ("AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING"), as does Table 18, but the specification table below it names the control "Audit Review, Analysis, and Reporting".
items.proposed: In the AU-6 specification table, change the control name to "Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting".

items.comment: The SC-15 heading at line 8005 ("COLLABORATIVE COMPUTING DEVICES") and the specification table below it ("Collaborative Computing Devices") use a shortened title. The SP 800-53 Rev. 5 title, also used in Table 18, is "Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications".
items.proposed: Change the heading at line 8005 to "SC-15 COLLABORATIVE COMPUTING DEVICES AND APPLICATIONS" and the table name to "Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications".

items.comment: The headings for AC-1 (line 6993, "ACCESS CONTROL POLICY AND PROCEDURES") and AU-1 (line 7188, page 229, "AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY POLICY AND PROCEDURES") prefix the family name. The other 16 families' -1 headings use the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 title "POLICY AND PROCEDURES" (for example AT-1 at line 7154 and SR-1 at line 8187).
items.proposed: Change the headings at lines 6993 and 7188 to "AC-1 POLICY AND PROCEDURES" and "AU-1 POLICY AND PROCEDURES".

items.comment: Within E.7, the family subsections are numbered with a single running counter instead of restarting under each family: E.7.1.1 (line 6985), E.7.3.2 (7181), E.7.4.3 (7230), E.7.5.4 (7304), E.7.6.5 (7372), E.7.7.6 (7443), E.7.8.7 (7529), E.7.9.8 (7558), E.7.11.9 (7612), E.7.13.10 (7726), E.7.14.11 (7812), E.7.16.12 (7875), E.7.17.13 (7939) and E.7.18.14 (8078). Separately, the Risk Assessment family opens with introductory text at lines 7835-7836 that has no subsection heading, unlike the other families with family-level text.
items.proposed: Renumber each family subsection as E.7.n.1 (for example E.7.3.1 Tailoring Considerations for the Audit Family). Consider adding a heading such as "E.7.15.1 Tailoring Considerations for the Risk Assessment Family" before line 7835.

items.comment: Fig. 21 defines a fixed format for each entry, but some entries depart from it, which makes the overlay harder to read and to process reliably: line 7127 gives enhancement (5) discussion text without the "OT Discussion:" label; line 7352 reads "No OT Discussion." instead of "No OT Discussion for this control."; lines 7829, 7831 and 7833 (PS-7, PS-8, PS-9) omit the "OT Discussion:" label; lines 7886, 7889, 7896 and 8130 use "Control Enhancements:" where all other entries, including those listing several enhancements such as line 7001, use "Control Enhancement:"; line 8160 reads "Rationale for adding SI-13 control to HIGH baseline" where the other rationales omit "control".
items.proposed: Apply the Fig. 21 format to these lines: add "OT Discussion:" at lines 7127, 7829, 7831 and 7833; use "No OT Discussion for this control." at line 7352; use "Control Enhancement:" at lines 7886, 7889, 7896 and 8130; and use "Rationale for adding SI-13 to HIGH baseline" at line 8160.

items.comment: IEC 62443-2-1 element identifiers in Table 19 are written in different forms: "Event1.9" and a bare "2.1" (Task P-3, page 294) beside "ORG 1.3"; "ORG2.2", "ORG1.6" and "EVENT 1.1." with a trailing period (Tasks P-7 and P-8, page 295) beside "EVENT 1.1" and "AVAIL 1.2".
items.proposed: Use one form throughout, for example "EVENT 1.9", "ORG 2.1", "ORG 2.2", "ORG 1.6" and "EVENT 1.1".

items.comment: The comment template for this draft appears to be adapted from another publication: the worksheet is named "Comments on Draft IR 8212"; the line-number validation accepts only 0 to 1356 (starting line) and 0 to 1440 (ending line), while this draft's line numbers run past 8,000; the page drop-down list stops at page 60; and the section drop-down list ends at "Appendix B" and includes entries for an "ISCMAx tool". Commenters on Appendices E and F cannot enter valid references without triggering validation errors.
items.proposed: Update the template's worksheet name, line-number limits, and page and section lists to match SP 800-82r4 ipd, or remove those validations.
